parsed.why: No statute criminalises trans identity, but documented transfemicide pattern, police arresting Pride participants, local cross-dressing bans, male-facility custody and service refusals; no national protection or working remedy. Elevated Risk.

Statutory self-ID, conversion-practices ban and long reformist, functioning institutions; but 229 police-recorded hate incidents, up 42%, and one in five trans people threatened. No state targeting. High Reduced Risk.

No criminalisation, 2007/2024 court recognition, third-gender markers; but implementation lags, provincial harassment and government-institution discrimination documented, and 2024-26 political hate speech with supporter threats.

Latent colonial felonies (to 14 years) sweep in trans women read as male, no gender-identity protection, but zero documented prosecutions since 2013, no anti-trans violence or police targeting, and a traditional gender-variant category.
Cross-dressing criminalised outright; anal sex up to life; no recognition; documented state extrajudicial killings and torture of LGBTQ people plus vigilante attacks and 17% acceptance. Severe Risk.
